why: Defect C is that the orders-history workload template pairs activeDeadlineSeconds=14400 (4h)
with a window whose partitions cost 4-37 min each, so a wide slice cannot finish itself.
Defect D is the consequence: a partition killed mid-flight commits canonical_lineage rows
that no later run can reconcile or delete, permanently costing that day.
Slice width was already reduced to six partitions to fit inside 14400s. That kept the
worst case at 222 min against a 240 min budget -- 18 min of headroom, which is not a
margin, it is a coin flip. This receipt records the second, independent mitigation:
raising activeDeadlineSeconds on the task-scoped slices so a deadline kill stops being
the reachable failure mode at all.

not_applied_to.s1: already Failed; left at 14400 as the preserved Defect C exhibit
not_applied_to.s3: already Complete under 14400; left as the measured baseline
not_applied_to.s6: parked repair slice, still gated on human approval; not re-armed here

action.mutability_note: activeDeadlineSeconds is one of the few mutable Job spec fields. The patch was accepted on the RUNNING s4 with no pod disruption: same pod oday-data-platform-orders-history-93cb9f94-s4-qxvsf, RESTARTS 0, age unchanged across the patch.
action.non_destructive: Raising a kill timer cannot alter, delete, or admit any record. It changes no window, no image, no ingestion semantics -- only how long a slice is allowed to finish work it was already going to do. It is reversible by patching the value back.
action.still_bounded: 28800s is not 'no deadline'. Six partitions at the 37 min observed ceiling is 222 min; 28800s (480 min) leaves ~2.2x margin while still bounding a genuinely hung run.

measured_partition_minutes.note: All orders partitions run by this task on 2026-07-28, in execution order.
measured_partition_minutes.s1_outcome: killed DeadlineExceeded after 13 of 16 partitions -- not a data failure

what_this_does_not_change: Six partitions per slice stays. The width was chosen so a slice fits its own budget, and
it still does -- with headroom now instead of without. Widening slices on the back of the
raised deadline would re-introduce the Defect C shape and is deliberately not done.
Slices still run one at a time and still wait SUSPENDED rather than merely queued: the
private-pool node pool has exactly one node and does not scale up, and activeDeadlineSeconds
counts from the Job's startTime rather than from pod scheduling.
No ingestion code, image digest, window, or view definition is touched.

verification.cluster_read_back: kubectl -n oday-dev get job ... -o jsonpath '{.spec.activeDeadlineSeconds}' returned 28800 for s4,s5,b1,b2,b3,b4 and 14400 for s1,s2,s3,s6
verification.windows_read_back: each slice's ODP_ORDERS_HISTORY_START/_END read back off the cluster and matched the planned windows
verification.pod_undisturbed: s4 pod ...-qxvsf remained 2/2 Running with 0 restarts before and after the patch
